claims.text: A tailored heat treatment can introduce a high density of ordered dislocation arrays in MnNiSi-based alloys.
Introducing ordered dislocation arrays will increase the strength of MnNiSi-based alloys.
Introducing ordered dislocation arrays will increase the ductility of MnNiSi-based alloys.
Introducing ordered dislocation arrays will preserve a large magnetocaloric effect in MnNiSi-based alloys.
As-cast or as-synthesized MnNiSi-based magnetic refrigerant alloys have a relatively coarse grain structure.
Untreated MnNiSi-based magnetic refrigerant alloys have relatively low ductility and inferior mechanical resilience.
Untreated MnNiSi-based magnetic refrigerant alloys exhibit a large magnetocaloric effect.
Controlled thermal or light thermomechanical processing can produce a uniform ordered-dislocation network without causing unwanted phase transformations.
The proposed treatment will produce a refined, homogeneous microstructure in addition to ordered dislocation arrays.
Ordered dislocations will impede crack propagation.
Ordered dislocations will enhance strain hardening.
Impeded crack propagation and enhanced strain hardening will improve toughness and ductility.
The introduced dislocations will be coherent and will not significantly alter the magnetic-domain configuration.
Avoiding significant changes to magnetic-domain configuration will retain the magnetocaloric entropy change associated with the phase transformation.
Processing must occur above a temperature sufficient for dislocation ordering but below a threshold that changes composition or disrupts magnetically active phases.
An inert processing atmosphere is needed to avoid oxidation.
Excessive dislocation accumulation or over-aging can cause secondary-phase formation or magnetic inhomogeneity.
Secondary-phase formation or magnetic inhomogeneity would degrade the magnetocaloric response.
The optimal processing window is narrow and varies with small composition fluctuations.
Ordered-dislocation engineering has produced beneficial magnetically driven functional behavior in a related magnetic shape-memory alloy.
